dash.name: Name

scan.title: Today's plans
scan.diag: Last scan: {total} in watchlist, {scanned} evaluated, {signals} signals, {plans} plans. Threshold {min}%.
scan.blocked_lot: {n} signal(s) were dropped because one lot already exceeds the risk budget. That is a capital constraint, not a strategy failure.
scan.hint: Plans expire at the next session close. Confirm execution on the receipt page so the system can track plan-vs-fill deviation.
receipt.title: Receipt
receipt.invalid_hint: Go back to Kestrel and generate a new plan.
receipt.recorded: The deviation will show up in your next review.
j.name: Name
j.no_open: No open positions. Pick a plan on the scan page and log the fill here.
j.discipline_hint: Compare clean trades with the ones where you broke your own rule. The gap is what your rules are worth.
ipo.name: IPO name
ipo.hint: Cash subscription is mostly a fee game: uSmart charges 0 per order, ZA Bank HK$50 non-refundable. Ten misses is real money.
fees.title: Cost calculator
fees.intro: Zero commission is not zero cost. Hong Kong adds stamp duty and four levies; the US only adds a platform fee.
fees.breakeven: Round-trip cost is {pct}% of the notional. That is how much the price must rise before you break even.
fees.hint: Rates change; always trust your broker statement. Add a broker by extending BrokerPlan in fees/calculator.py.
bt.title: Backtest
bt.intro: Check the same strategies against history. Backtest and live scan share one code path, so a rule change moves both.
bt.hint: Small samples lie. Fewer than 20 trades is a hint, not evidence.
settings.title: Settings
settings.glossary_hint: Underlined words show a plain-language note on hover.
settings.soon: This section opens in a later release.
footer.disclaimer: For research and learning only. Not investment advice. Markets carry risk.
footer.local: All data stays on this machine
scan.skipped_hint: “No daily bars” usually means a wrong ticker. Remove it on the dashboard and add it again — the app validates the code before saving.
scan.skip.no_bars: no daily bars — ticker is probably wrong
scan.rejected_title: {n} had a signal but were rejected:
scan.reject.low_reward: reward below 1.5 : 1 — not worth the risk
scan.reject.stop_too_tight: stop tighter than 1.5% — noise would take it out
scan.reject.lot_too_big: one lot already exceeds the risk budget (capital constraint)
market.title: Live quotes
market.sub: Latest price for your watchlist. Click a ticker for the detail page.
market.empty: Add a ticker above, e.g. 00700, AAPL or 腾讯.
market.hint: Quotes come from public endpoints and may lag a few seconds. Use the source link to verify.
market.stale: Some quotes are cached; a data source may be down.
adv.title: Advice
adv.auto_off: Auto scan is off — manual only
adv.learn: What / why now / what if wrong
adv.empty: Hit “Scan now”. No advice is also a conclusion: today is not the day.
settings.sub: Every switch lives here. Changes apply immediately.
settings.capital_hint: Every position and risk number is derived from this. Use the real figure.
settings.risk_hint: The amount you can lose without caring. 1–2 is sane.
settings.learning_hint: Expands every plan into what / why now / what if wrong.
settings.universe_hint: The pool is a size- and liquidity-ranked slice of each market. Picking needs it.
settings.pool_size_hint: Top N by market cap. 30–50 is usually enough.
settings.min_score_hint: 0.55 means a strategy must score 55% before it produces advice.
settings.auto_hint: Runs on the interval below when on.
settings.interval_hint: Daily strategies do not need to be frequent; 60 is fine.
settings.sources_meta: All three are unofficial public endpoints
settings.sources_hint: Disable one and quotes fall back to the next. All off falls back to Eastmoney.
settings.engine_mode_hint: Rules need no key. A model only adds explanation, never size.
settings.backup_hint: The database holds every trade, setting and scan.
settings.backup_warn: Import only inserts: existing rows are never overwritten.
cost.sub: Know exactly what a round trip costs, and how far price must move to break even.
cost.calc_title: How far must it rise to break even
cost.calc_meta: Zero commission is not zero cost
cost.note: HK has stamp duty plus four levies; US only platform fees. Fixed fees hurt small orders: 10k HKD is ~0.55%, 1k HKD becomes 3.7%.
cost.plans_hint: Edits here change the calculator and every plan's fee estimate. Built-ins can be disabled, not deleted.
sim.title: Quick backtest
sim.sub: Check whether the rules made money before you take their advice.
sim.intro: A backtest is not a forecast. It answers one question: how badly would this rule have lost?
journal.sub: Every real fill, and whether you followed the plan.
journal.import_intro: Copy fills from your broker app and paste them here.
journal.import_placeholder:
One per line, e.g.
2026-11-06 BUY 00700 100 shares @419.80
2026-11-06 SELL AAPL 1 share @342.37
journal.parse_empty: No fills recognised. Check for a side, a quantity and a price.
journal.ocr_missing: No OCR engine (tesseract) on this machine. Pasting text is more accurate anyway.
scan.reject.sector_cap: sector already represented — avoids one big sector bet
settings.max_sector_hint: Stops the screen from returning eight banks. Default 2.
sim.what: This is not a broker's paper-trading account. Nothing is matched or filled here. It replays the same rules over past prices and answers one question: what would have happened if you had followed them for the last two years?
sim.gate: Expectancy is the only number that matters here: what one unit of risk returns on average. Above zero it stays enabled; at or below zero it is switched off and stops appearing in advice.
sim.none: Hit “Recompute” to run it over cached daily bars.
sim.single_meta: How the rules behaved on a single stock
sim.result_intro: On this symbol the rules fired {n} times, won {win}% of them, for {total}R in total and {avg}R per trade.
sim.no_trades: The rules never triggered in this window.
settings.custom_source_hint: If the three built-ins stop working, point the app at your own endpoint. Custom sources are tried first.
settings.custom_source_fields: Paths use dots, e.g. data.quote.price or items.0.last. Leave blank for a plain-text number.
settings.preset_none: No preset — I'll fill it in
settings.preset_help: Pick a provider and the URL and field paths fill themselves in. You only add the key.
horizon.title: Trading horizon
horizon.hint: Sets which bars the scan reads, how long a backtest may hold, and how long a plan stays valid.
horizon.auto_on: Picked from the tape, your capital and your positions
horizon.beta_hint: Monthly bars are a trend reference only: no fundamentals, thinnest sample. Not a full long-term strategy.
horizon.insufficient: No cached history yet — run a scan first.
sim.horizon_hint: A different horizon means different bars, and a different holding period.
rules.horizon_hint: A rule that loses on daily bars can still work weekly; verdicts are kept per horizon.
today.title: Today
today.quiet_body: No position risk and no pending advice. Sitting still is also a decision.
today.no_watch_body: Add one on the Markets page, e.g.
today.step1_title: Tell it how much you have
today.step1_body: Settings → General: capital and loss per trade. Every share count is derived from these.
today.step2_body: It picks names that fit your horizon and capital, then sizes the stop, target and shares.
today.step3_body: Press “I bought it”, enter the real price and quantity. The journal shows the gap.
today.why_body: A 50% loss needs a 100% gain to recover. So this tool sizes the stop and the position before it talks about picking — people who do it in the other order mostly pay fees.
welcome.intro: Three questions, one minute. The answers decide what it suggests — including whether it suggests you do nothing today.
welcome.q1: How much do you have, and how much can you lose?
welcome.q1_hint: Share counts are derived from the loss you can tolerate, not from conviction. Beginners: 1–2% per trade.
welcome.capital_hint: Used only for sizing. Not uploaded, not linked to any account.
welcome.risk_help: With {capital} capital, {risk}% means at most {amount} per trade.
welcome.q2_hint: Pick any. Unselected markets are never scanned and never appear in advice.
welcome.q3: How long do you plan to hold?
welcome.q3_hint: The horizon sets the bars, the stop width and the plan lifetime. Choose auto if unsure — it decides from the tape and your capital.
welcome.h_auto_note: Re-decided before each scan, with the reason shown
welcome.h_short_note: Days to weeks; higher turnover, fee sensitive
welcome.h_medium_note: Weeks to two months; less churn
welcome.h_long_note: Managed on monthly bars; thinnest sample
welcome.footnote: It does not place orders and promises no profits. It does three things: quantify the risk, write the plan down, and compare what you actually did with it.
welcome.title: Welcome to {name}
adv.no_history_body: Advice appears here once it is acted on or expires.
adv.no_scan_body: Press “Start scan” in the top right.
journal.no_positions_body: Press “I bought it” on the Advice page, or record one here. Every position gets stop distance and open P&L automatically.
journal.fill_intro: Record it here whether you followed advice or not. Use the numbers from your broker's fill note.
welcome.m_cn_note: T+1, price limits, stamp duty on sells only
welcome.m_hk_note: Traded in lots, stamp duty both sides
journal.require_fill: Ticker, quantity and price are all required.
adv.ai_note: The rule engine still feeds the model the measured record of every path, but no longer publishes advice. To test a rule on its own, go to
stock.no_bars: No daily bars yet — this symbol has probably never been scanned.
receipt.expired_body: The advice has expired. Recording it now would book today's trade against an old plan — check the latest advice on your machine.
receipt.deviation_hint: Negative means you paid less than suggested, positive means you paid more. Over time this matters more than stock picking.
receipt.fill_hint: Enter your actual fill price and quantity. Differing from the suggestion is fine — this records what happened.
sim.full_data: Full data, fold detail and the rule editor live on the
sim.symbol_hint: Any symbol works: type a ticker or MARKET/TICKER. Missing history is fetched automatically.
settings.risk_help: Percent of capital risked per trade. Beginners 1–2%; set your own once you have a record.
settings.exposure_hint: Total across all positions. 0 means no limit, which is not recommended.
settings.market_cn_hint: T+1, price limits, stamp duty on sells
settings.market_hk_hint: Traded in lots, stamp duty both sides
settings.test_sent: Test message sent. Check WeChat or your phone.
settings.bridge_root_hint: Empty follows the data directory. In containers point it at a shared path; the prompts above use whichever path is configured.
rules.title: Screening rules
rules.sub: A rule is data, not code. Anyone can add one; the validator decides whether it earns a place.
rules.ai_notice_title: Advice currently comes from {engine}; rules no longer pick directly.
rules.ai_notice_body: They still feed the model the measured record of every path, and they remain the tool for understanding market structure. You can validate any rule on its own at any time. To let rules pick again:
rules.rules_notice_title: Advice comes from the rule engine.
rules.rules_notice_body: Every rule runs the same walk-forward test against holding the same entry with no stop. Anything without excess return is switched off automatically, and kept for retesting.
rules.verdict_intro: Verdicts measure excess return: same entry, same holding period, no stop. Beating it is the only thing that counts. Making money in a bull market proves nothing.
rules.note: Note (why it is built this way)
rules.for_ai: Let another AI write a rule
rules.for_ai_meta: Machine-readable · paste it into any model
rules.for_ai_body: This prompt spells out the fields, operators, semantics, hard constraints and worked examples. Paste it into any model to get a valid rule, then paste the result into “Write a rule”; saving compiles and validates it.
rules.how_to_write_body: A rule is “enter only when every condition holds”. The score bonus only ranks survivors; it never changes whether a trade is taken.
rules.operators: Operators: > >= < <= between is_true is_false. `right` can be a number or another field name (e.g. high20), which compares the two.
settings.scan_meta: These apply to both the rule engine and the model
settings.cs_yahoo: Add Yahoo as a built-in fallback
settings.engine_base_hint: Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint: DeepSeek, Qwen, a local Ollama.
settings.engine_budget_hint: When the budget runs out it stops and says so. It never quietly falls back to rules — that would mean you think you are using a model when you are not.
settings.wb_title: WorkBuddy needs no URL and no API key.
settings.rule_engine_hint: Conditions live in editable JSON: reproducible, auditable, and every rule carries a measured record. Rules without demonstrated edge are switched off. No external calls, no cost, instant.
settings.rule_engine_limit: The limit: it can only express what you thought of in advance.
settings.llm_note: The model gets the full indicator set, your account constraints and every rule's measured record. It picks, argues, and sets stops and targets. Local code validates each number and discards what fails with a logged reason; position size is always computed locally from the risk budget. Each run costs roughly tens of thousands of tokens.
settings.wb_body: The app writes tasks to a queue; a WorkBuddy cron job answers them and the result is ingested automatically. It is asynchronous — expect minutes, not seconds.
settings.wb_need_cron: Create a cron job in WorkBuddy to consume it — copy the prompt below as-is.
settings.wb_job1_hint: Run every 30–60 minutes. It reads the queue and writes answers; the app collects them.
settings.wb_job2_hint: Run every 5–15 minutes, together with the WorkBuddy notification channel.
settings.auto_check_hint: Checks and tells you; never installs behind your back. Turn it off and only the button above checks.
settings.paths_hint: Settings → Backup exports a full snapshot. Moving machines is just dropping it into the new data directory.
settings.license_body: GPL-3.0. Use it, change it, share it — forks must ship under the same licence. It gives no investment advice and places no orders; the decisions are yours.
settings.wb_channel_hint: This channel relies on a WorkBuddy cron job to forward files to WeChat. Paste the prompt below into a new cron job — the paths already reflect the outbox you configured.
journal.confirm_stop: Move the stop up to {stop}? A stop may only move up; it cannot be undone.
journal.parsed_ok: Parsed {n} line(s). Check them, then import.
journal.stop_required: A stop is not optional: without it, distance-to-stop and exit advice cannot be computed. If unsure, take the stop from the advice card.
journal.price_meta: Prices from the last quote refresh
journal.expired_line: {n} advice items reached a decision: {a} executed, {b} skipped, {c} expired. Drift is fill minus suggested entry; negative means you paid less.
